Step 1: Install Docker
Docker is a containerization platform that allows you to package your application along with its dependencies into a single, portable container. This ensures consistency across different environments. Installation Steps: 1. Log in to your server via SSH. 2. Update the package list: bash sudo apt-get update 3. Install Docker: bash sudo apt-get install docker.io 4. Start and enable Docker service: bash sudo systemctl start docker sudo systemctl enable docker

Conclusion
Writebook by 37signals is a powerful, free, self-hosted web publishing platform designed for writers, publishers, and content creators. Its features such as Markdown support, flexible page layouts, granular privacy, collaborative writing, and seamless progress syncing make it an ideal choice for various use cases beyond technical documentation. By following the detailed steps provided in this guide, you can easily set up your own instance of Writebook on a lightweight server environment. The open source nature of the platform provides developers with the flexibility to modify and extend its functionality, further enhancing its capabilities and potential applications. Whether you're creating technical runbooks, employee handbooks, product instruction manuals, creative writing, or family histories, Writebook offers a simple, distraction-free platform for publishing long-form content with full ownership of your work.
